source_review.notes: Checked current ISO 15288:2023, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 catalog metadata; NASA handbook and ConOps appendix; SEBoK 2.14 System Requirements and Stakeholder Needs Definition pages; and NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1. NASA, SEBoK, and NIST links returned HTTP 200; three ISO pages returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client but current official metadata and the 29148 operational-scenario definition were independently retrieved.

evidence: Reviewed scenario and context-relation tuples, context set/relation definition, mode- and actor-indexed transition representation, coverage matrix, and gap predicate.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols are introduced before use; context representations, scenario intent, deterministic or branching transitions, coverage presence, and validation evidence remain distinct.

evidence: Executed scenario-coverage-check under Python 3.14.4 and independently recomputed four scenarios, one nominal and three off-nominal, four distinct actors, five distinct requirements, and each missing-field result.
Verified sorted missing-precondition S-maintenance, missing-recovery S-network-loss, missing-trace S-fire, and false declared coverage completion.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts establish only properties of the four declared records; no operational completeness or adequacy is inferred.

evidence: Checked state-transition indexing over events, modes, actors, and environment and verified that it permits branching/uncertainty rather than asserting determinism.
Re-derived the zero-column coverage-gap predicate and its one-way interpretation as a gap candidate.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: A nonzero coverage column never proves depth, realism, correctness, independence, or completeness.

evidence: Reviewed omitted non-users, external-external common causes, current/transition/target context, missing preconditions, asynchronous and concurrent events, delayed or corrupt interfaces, mode disagreement, overload, human workload, accessibility, maintenance, emergency, recovery debt, migration, and retirement.
Challenged all ten examples and five answers for solution bias, happy-path bias, premature end state, unsupported validation, and missing authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Scenario families expose declared conditions but do not enumerate unknown or unrepresented stakeholders, interactions, or environments.

evidence: Traced purpose, interaction, temporal, stakeholder, and evidence invariants through exposition, ten worked examples, and five complete answers.
Verified bidirectional links among scenario steps and candidate requirements, interfaces, assumptions, hazards, architecture, verification, validation, and operating evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: Direct actors, affected non-users, support roles, and governing authorities remain distinct; every consequential thread includes recovery and end obligations.

proof_review.notes: The chapter defines modeling and coverage rules but presents no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed uses of complete, adequate, representative, validate, verify, causal, safe, compliant, independent, operational, and evidence.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-009/report.json records exact local execution evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes declared-record coverage only. It cannot validate scenario semantics, axes, stakeholder completeness, human behavior, operational realism, safety, compliance, or outcomes.

conceptual_review.notes: Professor-style review checked system/context distinction, purpose-specific views, operational concept and ConOps, scenario anatomy, modes, temporal/causal branching, lifecycle, human roles, mission threads, traceability, coverage, and validation boundaries for conceptual consistency.

practitioner_review.notes: Practitioner-style review checked water response, record migration, elevator emergency, checkout, communications diversity, medical maintenance, public benefits, requirement trace, concurrent control-room incidents, service retirement, charging, remote consultation, warehouse robots, payment repair, and railway doors. Each example exposes assumptions, operational reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Pedagogical review confirmed progression from context framing through typed relations, temporal contexts, operational intent, branches/modes, human work, end states, lifecycle, scenario families, traceability, executable coverage, and validation. Ten examples and five complete answers require modeling, diagnosis, matrix design, repair, and high-consequence review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
